history.value: Sutter Hill Ventures is one of the oldest venture firms still operating: it dates its founding to 1962, and Bill Draper and Paul Wythes led its early years in Palo Alto. Its bets include Nvidia, NetApp and Activision, and it incubated Pure Storage (now Everpure) and Snowflake in its own offices. It invests from one evergreen partnership and an opportunity fund, together about $3.7 billion.

investment_concept.value: Sutter Hill Ventures forms and funds technology companies from their first day, often in its own offices, and backs them for decades.
investment_concept.basis: Derived, flagged: the firm publishes no statement (its site is an animated wordmark, 'SHV', and an address; meta description 'Founded 1962 · Palo Alto, California', read 2026-09-28). The line rests on the incubation pattern in the base (Pure Storage, Snowflake, Sigma, Observe, Luminary Cloud, Augment formed around the firm's managing directors, several in its own offices) and on its single evergreen partnership. PRO-147: the thesis is the firm's own crisp statement (Erik, 2026-09-26); this is the exception for a firm that makes none.

investment_stage.basis: DERIVED: the firm publishes no positioning. Series A is the core: 51 of the 94 members whose round is on record entered at a named Series A, most of them companies the firm formed or first funded (Pure Storage, Sigma, Observe, Augment, Matic). Growth is real (34 rows: later rounds such as Astera Labs' Series B, PacBio's Series E, DataRobot, Ramp, and the 1962 Opportunity Fund's positions) and Seed is small (9 rows, Snowflake's 2012 Series Seed among them). 180 members, mostly the 1970 to 2000 book, have no round on record.

investment_geo.basis: 266 of 274 members are US companies, nearly all in the Bay Area. The rest are single companies (UK 3, China 3 including Youku Tudou and YaoLan, Ireland 1, New Zealand 1), too few for an 'other' label. The firm reported opening a London office in 2021 (Business Insider, 2021-10-25), which the 2026 ADV does not list.

investment_scope.basis: DERIVED from the grind's focus column: seven values clear the 12-company floor (about 4.5% of 274): Healthcare & Bio 68, Data Infrastructure 51, SaaS 44, Industrial & Robotics 29, Media, Gaming & Advertising 25, Consumer & Marketplaces 17, Fintech & Payments 13. Below it: Security 9, DevTools & APIs 7, AI & Applied AI 4, Climate & Energy 3; 4 rows sit outside the taxonomy. The firm's own 2004 to 2016 sector filters (Software, Healthcare, Networking & Computer Technology, Business & Financial Services, Consumer, Investment Partnerships) agree in shape.

investment_range.basis: MEDIAN $12.25M, published as $12M: the median entry round over 129 members whose entry round is on record with an amount (103 from the documented funding history the judges recorded, 26 from the first Form D naming a firm person; p10 $2.1M, p25 $5.8M, p75 $25M, p90 $64M). A round size, not a cheque size. LOWER $0.9M: Snowflake's August 2012 Series Seed, of which Sutter Hill bought about 48% (its own Form 3), the smallest documented entry. UPPER $375M: Sila's June 2024 Series G, which Sutter Hill led (Bloomberg 2024-09-24; GeekWire 2026-07-21), inside 10 to 15% of the partnership's $2.94B gross assets. Rejected: Ramp's $500M Series E-2 (Sutter Hill joined, did not lead).

notable_investments.basis: The five best known of the firm's companies, most recognised first, by a general reader (PRO-152, Erik 2026-09-24): Nvidia (the 1993 Series A with Sequoia), Snowflake (incubated 2012), Activision (1979), Palm (Palm Computing, acquired by US Robotics 1995, later HP), Glassdoor (bought by Recruit 2018). Also well known: Pure Storage (now Everpure), NetApp, Shutterfly.
